questions.stem: What does success mean in general terms when applied to data solutions?
options: Spending the entire project budget
Storing as much data as possible
Achieving a goal or doing something well
Finishing a project ahead of schedule regardless of outcome
Using the newest available technology
questions.explanation: Success, in general, means achieving a goal or doing something well, like hitting a target.

questions.stem: Which analogy is used for working on a data solution without a clear definition of success?
options: Trying to win a game without knowing the rules or the score
Driving a car without fuel
Building a house without bricks
Reading a book in the dark
Cooking without a recipe
questions.explanation: Working without a definition of success is compared to trying to win a game without knowing the rules or the score.

questions.stem: How are data solutions described when discussing the definition of success?
options: Hardware for storing backups
Legal agreements about data sharing
Reports produced for regulators
Software licences for databases
Ways to manage and use information, including collecting, organising and analysing data
questions.explanation: Data solutions are ways to handle and use information effectively, including tasks like collecting, organising and analysing data.

questions.stem: When success is defined for a data solution, what kinds of goals might be set?
options: Goals about office location and staffing
Goals related to accuracy, efficiency, security or other aspects of managing data
Goals about the colour scheme of dashboards
Goals about the number of vendors used
Goals about the age of the hardware
questions.explanation: Defining success means setting goals, which could relate to accuracy, efficiency, security or other aspects of managing data.

questions.stem: Which image is used to describe how a definition of success helps with monitoring progress?
options: A clock counting down
A scoreboard at a stadium
A thermometer showing temperature
A map showing where you are and how far you are from your destination
A ladder with numbered rungs
questions.explanation: Knowing what success looks like is like having a map that shows where you are on your journey and how far you are from your destination.

questions.stem: How does a clear definition of success help with decision-making in data solutions?
options: You know what you are aiming for, so you can choose the best strategies and tools to get there
It removes the need to consult stakeholders
It guarantees that no decision will ever need revisiting
It lets you skip testing
It allows decisions to be delegated entirely to software
questions.explanation: With a clear definition of success you know what you are aiming for, so you can make informed decisions about strategies and tools.

questions.stem: What is said about defining success as part of continuous improvement?
options: It should be done once at project kick-off and never changed
It only matters after the solution has failed
It is the responsibility of auditors, not the project team
It is an ongoing process in which goals can be adjusted and solutions improved over time
It should be avoided because goals slow teams down
questions.explanation: Defining success is not a one-time thing; it is an ongoing process in which goals are adjusted as needed and data solutions keep improving.

questions.stem: If success for a data solution project means having accurate and up-to-date information, what follows?
options: The project only needs to run once
Accuracy can be ignored once the data is loaded
Processes and systems are designed for accuracy, and the data is regularly checked and updated
All historical data must be deleted
The data must be moved to the cloud
questions.explanation: In that example, processes and systems are designed to ensure accuracy, and the data is regularly checked and updated to maintain it.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT given as a reason why defining success matters for data solutions?
options: It helps set goals
It helps monitor progress
It supports informed decisions
It enables continuous improvement
It removes the need to monitor progress
questions.explanation: Defining success supports setting goals, monitoring progress, informed decisions and continuous improvement; it does not remove the need to monitor progress.

questions.stem: In summary, defining success for a data solution is compared to what?
options: Buying insurance against failure
Setting clear goals and having a roadmap
Hiring more staff
Writing a technical specification
Choosing a database vendor
questions.explanation: Defining success is like setting clear goals and having a roadmap, helping you stay on track, make better decisions and keep improving.
